2026-12-13.title: Third Sunday of Advent (Gaudete Sunday)
readings: The spirit of the Lord God is upon me; I will greatly rejoice in the Lord
My soul rejoices in my God
Among you stands one whom you do not know
2026-12-13.alt: Gaudete Sunday. Rose vestments may be worn; the rose candle of the Advent wreath is lit. The memorial of St Lucy is not celebrated this year because it falls on Sunday.
2026-12-13.verse: John answered them, “I baptize with water. Among you stands one whom you do not know, the one who is coming after me; I am not worthy to untie the thong of his sandal.”
theo: The Entrance Antiphon gives this Sunday its name: “Gaudete in Domino semper”, “Rejoice in the Lord always; again I say, rejoice. The Lord is near” (Philippians 4:4–5). Halfway through Advent the violet softens to rose. Joy is not a break from Advent; it is its heart, because the One we await is already near.

Isaiah's servant says, “The spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me, because the LORD has anointed me to bring good news to the oppressed, to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives.” Jesus will read these very words in the synagogue at Nazareth and say, “Today this scripture has been fulfilled” (Luke 4:21). The response today is Mary's Magnificat: Christian joy is the joy of the humble whom God has lifted up.

John the Evangelist presents the Baptist as a witness: “He himself was not the light, but he came to testify to the light.” When priests and Levites ask who he is, John answers with three “No”s: not the Messiah, not Elijah, not the prophet. He is only “the voice”. Then he says something every Advent needs to hear: “Among you stands one whom you do not know.” Christ is already in our midst, in the Word, the sacraments, the poor, the person beside us; the question is whether we recognise him.

Paul gives the programme for joyful waiting: “Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all circumstances… Do not quench the Spirit… Hold fast to what is good.” And he ends with a promise: “The one who calls you is faithful, and he will do this.” Holiness is God's work in us; our joy rests on his faithfulness.
conn: Rose (not pink) vestments are worn only twice a year: Gaudete Sunday in Advent and Laetare Sunday in Lent. The colour signals that the penitential season is half over and the feast is near.
The Latin word means “Rejoice!” (plural imperative), the first word of the Entrance Antiphon from Philippians 4:4.
John denies being the Messiah, Elijah, or the Prophet (Deuteronomy 18:15). His one positive claim is to be a voice (Isaiah 40:3). A voice exists for the sake of the word it carries.
Jesus' inaugural sermon in Luke 4:16–21 reads Isaiah 61:1–2, stopping before “the day of vengeance of our God”. He proclaims the year of favour.
Today the response is not a psalm but Mary's song (Luke 1:46–55), sung daily at Vespers throughout the Church.
“Among you stands one whom you do not know.”
St Augustine saw in this verse Christ's hidden presence: he is near even when unrecognised.
altar: At every Mass the deacon or priest says, “The Lord be with you.” It is John's message turned into a greeting: Christ stands among us.
Before Communion we hear, “Behold the Lamb of God”, the words John the Baptist spoke when he saw Jesus (John 1:29). The voice points; the Word is given.
outline: Light the rose candle. Ask: what is your reason to rejoice this week?

Isaiah 61, fulfilled in Jesus at Nazareth.
Joy of the humble, like Mary's Magnificat.
Point 3 · One whom you do not know
Christ is already among us; recognise him.
The rose candle in the middle of violet: joy in the middle of waiting.
live: Each night this week, name three things that made you rejoice.
Pray a short prayer each time you wash your hands or pick up your phone.
Look for Christ in one person you usually overlook.
Bring good news to the poor (Isaiah 61:1)
Visit a lonely or sick person before Christmas.
fathers: “John was the voice; Christ is the Word. The voice passes; the Word remains.”
He writes that the joy of Advent is the joy of a heart that knows the Lord is coming to it.
He notes John's humility: questioned about his greatness, he answered by pointing to another.
magis: The joy of the Gospel fills the hearts of those who encounter Jesus.
John, the voice of the Spirit.
saints: 14 Dec: St John of the Cross. 17 Dec: the O Antiphons begin; the final days of Advent.
2026-12-13.prayer: O God, who see how your people faithfully await the feast of the Lord's Nativity, enable us, we pray, to attain the joys of so great a salvation and to celebrate them always with solemn worship and glad rejoicing. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Joy is the heart of Advent: the Lord is near.
Christ fulfilled Isaiah's good news to the poor.
He stands among us, often unrecognised.
2026-12-13.action: Name three reasons for joy each night this week.
2026-12-13.question: Where is Christ among us whom I do not recognise?
2026-12-13.special: Third Sunday of Advent, Gaudete Sunday. Colour: rose or violet.
illus: In Kerala homes the Christmas star goes up in the middle of Advent, before the feast itself. It does not mean Christmas has come; it announces that it is near. That is Gaudete Sunday.

family.explain: John the Baptist was a voice telling everyone that Jesus was near. He said Jesus was already among them, though they did not know him.
family.intention: We pray to recognise Jesus in each other.
family.ask: Ask: “Where did we see Jesus this week in someone's kindness?”

kidsaint: A young girl of Sicily who gave her riches to the poor and died a martyr. Her name means “light”. Lesson: be a light for others.
term: Latin for “Rejoice!”; the name of the Third Sunday of Advent, from the Entrance Antiphon (Philippians 4:4).

pm.open: Rejoice in the Lord always; again I say, rejoice. The Lord is near. Lord Jesus, on this Gaudete Sunday fill our gathering with your joy. Amen.
share: Paul says: rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all circumstances (1 Thessalonians 5:16–18). Which of these is hardest for me?
John said: I am not the Messiah (John 1:20). How do I point others to Jesus rather than to myself?
What gives me true joy this Advent?
interc: For the Church, that she may be a witness of joy in a sad world.
For those who cannot rejoice because of grief, illness or poverty.
For the poor and the brokenhearted, to whom good news is promised (Isaiah 61:1).
For prisoners and captives, that they may find freedom.
For our group, that we may rejoice, pray and give thanks always.
pm.close: Lord God, the coming of your Son is near. Fill us with joy, teach us to give thanks in all things, and make us witnesses to the light. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today is Gaudete Sunday, the Sunday of joy. The priest may wear rose vestments, and we light the rose candle. Why? Because the Lord is near.

The prophet Isaiah says: “The spirit of the Lord is upon me; he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor, to bind up the broken-hearted, to proclaim liberty to captives.” Years later Jesus stood in the synagogue of Nazareth, read these words, and said: “Today this scripture has been fulfilled.” Our joy has a name: Jesus.

Instead of a psalm we sing Mary's song: “My soul rejoices in my God.” Mary was poor and humble, and God did great things for her. Christian joy is not the joy of having everything; it is the joy of being loved by God.

In the Gospel people ask John: “Who are you? Are you the Messiah? Elijah? The prophet?” And he says, “No, no, no. I am only a voice.” And then: “Among you stands one whom you do not know.” Jesus was already there, in the crowd, unnoticed.
Is it the same with us? Jesus is among us: in the Eucharist, in the Word, in the poor at our gate, in the family member we take for granted. Advent asks us to open our eyes.

St Paul gives us a simple programme for this week: “Rejoice always, pray without ceasing, give thanks in all circumstances.” Try it: every night, thank God for three joys. And remember his promise: “The one who calls you is faithful, and he will do this.” Rejoice: the Lord is near!
kids: Children, today the candle is pink, I mean rose! It's the candle of joy.
Christmas is getting close, and Jesus is near!
John the Baptist said: Jesus is among you, but you don't know him. Where can we find Jesus? In church, in our family, in poor people.
This week, say thank you to God for three happy things every night!

intro: Christ fulfils Isaiah's good news, gives the joy of the humble, and stands among us unrecognised.

sub: Isaiah's servant is anointed by the Spirit.
Our joy has a name: Jesus.
q: The spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me, because the LORD has anointed me; he has sent me to bring good news to the oppressed, to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and release to the prisoners; to proclaim the year of the LORD's favor, and the day of vengeance of our God; to comfort all who mourn.

The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor. He has sent me to proclaim release to the captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to let the oppressed go free, to proclaim the year of the Lord's favor.

points.h: One whom you do not know
sub: We must learn to recognise him.
q: I will greatly rejoice in the LORD, my whole being shall exult in my God; for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation, he has covered me with the robe of righteousness.
John answered them, “I baptize with water. Among you stands one whom you do not know, the one who is coming after me; I am not worthy to untie the thong of his sandal.”
